mainTopic: The third and fourth פייסות, why the קטורת goes to new כהנים, the afternoon תמיד lottery, and how the Sages reach four lotteries
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing an earlier point: a ברייתא teaches that the כהן placed the פדר (fat) over the cut neck out of respect. A new משנה then lists the third פייס, for the קטורת, which was open only to new כהנים. It also lists the fourth פייס, for carrying the limbs from the כבש to the מזבח, which was open to everyone. The גמרא explains that no one offered the קטורת twice because, as רבי חנינא says, it brings wealth. אביי explains why the עולה, mentioned in the same verse, does not bring wealth: it is common, while the קטורת is rare. That verse leads to רבא's teaching that scholars who rule on הלכה come from לוי and יששכר. Next, רבי יוחנן rules that there was no separate afternoon פייס for the תמיד, and the גמרא defends him against several ברייתות, ending with the answer that שבת is different because the משמרות change. Finally, the גמרא shows that the fourth פייס does not follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and explains the reason for their dispute. רבא then shows how each Sage still reaches four lotteries, and a discussion of a תנא who counts five begins and continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: What does mentioning the fat come to teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the earlier mention of the פדר (fat) together with the head comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does this come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the earlier source bothered to mention the פדר together with the head. This is a setup question, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the source said the כהן carrying the head also carried the פדר with it. The גמרא assumes no detail is extra, so it asks what practical lesson that detail teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: For what purpose does it come? (What does it teach?)

phrases.english: For what does it come (to teach)?
phrases.notes: Refers back to the mention of the פדר with the head of the קרבן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion earlier about carrying the limbs.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson is taught by mentioning the פדר together with the head?

steps.title: The fat is placed over the cut, out of respect
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the כהן laid the פדר over the place of slaughter when carrying the head up. This is the respectful way.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: How would he do it? He would place the fat over the place of slaughter and carry it up. That is the respectful way toward the One Above.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The fat is mentioned with the head because the כהן covered the bloody cut of the neck with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The detail teaches a matter of דרך כבוד (respect), not just logistics. Bringing an exposed, bloody cut up to the מזבח would be undignified, so the fat covers it.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
The layer of fat of the animal
The place of slaughter (the cut neck)

steps.whatToRemember: The פדר covers the cut of the neck when the head is carried up. This is done for כבוד (respect).

phrases.english: For that which was taught: How would he do it?
He places the fat upon the place of slaughter
and brings it up,

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶה הוּא דֶּרֶךְ כָּבוֹד שֶׁל מַעְלָה.
phrases.english: and this is the respectful way toward the One Above.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The mention teaches that the fat is placed over the cut of the neck, out of respect.

steps.title: Third lottery: only new priests for the incense
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that the third פייס was for the קטורת, and only כהנים who had never offered it could take part.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The third lottery: 'Those who are new to the incense, come and join the lottery.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes the third lottery, which was open only to כהנים who had never offered the קטורת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other lotteries were open to everyone. Here a כהן who had already offered the קטורת was excluded. The גמרא will soon explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: Lottery used to assign Temple jobs
New ones (who never did this service)

phrases.english: MISHNA: The third lottery:
'Those new to the incense, come and draw lots.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה continuing the list of lotteries.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The third פייס, for the קטורת, is open only to כהנים who never offered it before.

steps.title: Fourth lottery: new and old priests together
steps.stepSummary: The fourth פייס, open to all כהנים, decided who would carry the limbs from the כבש up to the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the fourth: new ones together with old ones. Who will bring the limbs up from the ramp to the altar?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the fourth lottery. It was open to everyone and decided who would carry the limbs up to the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the קטורת lottery, there is no limit to new כהנים here. The limbs had been left earlier on the כבש (ramp), and now they were brought up onto the altar.

keyTerms.meaning: Old ones (who already did the service)
The ramp leading up to the altar

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the limbs carried in the second lottery. Those were brought to the כבש. This lottery is for bringing them from the כבש up onto the מזבח.

phrases.english: And the fourth: new ones together with old ones —
who brings up the limbs
from the ramp to the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with the next lottery.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fourth פייס, open to all כהנים, assigns carrying the limbs from the כבש to the מזבח.

steps.title: No priest ever offered the incense twice
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that no כהן ever offered the קטורת a second time.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A Sage taught: No person ever did it twice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by quoting a ברייתא that adds to the משנה. In practice, no כהן ever repeated the קטורת service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said that new כהנים were invited. The ברייתא adds that there were always enough new כהנים, so nobody ever did it a second time.

keyTerms.meaning: Never did it a second time

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught:
No person ever repeated it (the incense).

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: מֵעוֹלָם לֹא שָׁנָה אָדָם בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא expanding on the third lottery.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No כהן ever offered the קטורת twice.

steps.title: Why the insistence on new priests?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why they insisted that no כהן repeat the קטורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the rule that no one repeats the קטורת. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No other service has this restriction, so something special about the קטורת must explain it.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ברייתא in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why must the קטורת always go to a new כהן?

steps.title: Because the incense brings wealth
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא explains that offering the קטורת brings wealth, so it was spread among as many כהנים as possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: Because it brings wealth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא gives the reason: offering the קטורת makes a person rich. So they gave this blessing to a new כהן each time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the service carries a blessing of wealth, fairness demands spreading the opportunity. That explains why only new כהנים could enter this lottery.
steps.whatToRemember: The קטורת was given only to new כהנים because, according to רבי חנינא, it brings wealth (מעשרת).

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina said:
Because it brings wealth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The קטורת brings wealth, so the opportunity is shared.

steps.title: רב פפא asks for the source that incense brings wealth
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי for the source that the קטורת brings wealth. He suggests a verse in ברכת משה that is followed by 'ברך ה׳ חילו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: What is the reason? If you say it is because it is written, 'They shall put incense before You,' and right after it is written, 'Bless, O Lord, his substance'…
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא wants to know where the idea that קטורת brings wealth comes from. He proposes a possible source, which he is about to challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proposed source is the next verse. Right after the קטורת is mentioned, the תורה says 'ברך ה׳ חילו', a blessing of wealth. The word אילימא shows that this suggestion is being set up so it can be attacked.

keyTerms.meaning: If you would say (introduces a suggestion to be rejected)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
What is the reason?
If you say it is because it is written:
'They shall put incense before You,'
and it is written after it:
'Bless, O Lord, his substance,'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: מַאי טַעְמָא? אִילֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the source for רבי חנינא's claim.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What verse teaches that קטורת brings wealth?

steps.title: Then burnt-offerings should also bring wealth
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges the suggested source. The same verse also mentions the עולה, so by that logic the עולה should also bring wealth.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a burnt-offering too should bring wealth, for it is written: 'And whole burnt-offerings on Your altar'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks the suggested source. If being next to 'ברך ה׳ חילו' gives wealth, then the עולה, which is in the same verse, should also give wealth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse mentions both קטורת and כליל (the עולה) before the blessing. Nobody says the עולה brings wealth or limits it to new כהנים, so the proposed source proves too much.

phrases.english: If so, a burnt-offering also (should bring wealth),
for it is written: 'And whole burnt-offerings on Your altar'!
phrases.notes: Second half of דברים לג:י, the same verse as the קטורת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source proposed in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that 'ברך ה׳ חילו' is the source that קטורת brings wealth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse places the עולה right next to the קטורת. If closeness to the blessing gives wealth, the עולה should also bring wealth, but it is not treated that way.

steps.title: The burnt-offering is common, the incense is rare
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the עולה is offered often while the קטורת is offered rarely, so the blessing of wealth belongs to the קטורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This one is common, and that one is not common.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב פפא's challenge, which asked why the עולה should not also bring wealth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many עולות were brought every day, so the כהנים offering them were always changing. A blessing given to so many people would not single anyone out. The קטורת was offered only twice a day, so the special blessing of wealth makes sense for it alone.
steps.whatToRemember: The verse's blessing of wealth is linked to the קטורת because it is rare. The עולה is too common to carry it.

phrases.english: He (Abaye) said to him:
This one (the burnt-offering) is common, and that one (the incense) is not common.
phrases.notes: הָא… וְהָא = this one… and that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between the two cases (common versus rare)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the verse mentions both קטורת and עולה, both should bring wealth.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rare קטורת carries the blessing. The common עולה does not.

steps.title: Teaching scholars come from לוי or יששכר
steps.stepSummary: רבא states that a young scholar who gives halachic rulings comes only from שבט לוי or שבט יששכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You will not find a young scholar who gives rulings unless he comes from the tribe of לוי or the tribe of יששכר.
steps.whatsHappening: The verse just discussed (ישימו קטורה, דברים לג:י) opens with the words יורו משפטיך. Those words lead into a new teaching by רבא about which tribes produce scholars who rule on הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a side topic sparked by the same verse in ברכת משה. רבא makes a claim about where people who give הוראה come from. His sources follow in the next step.

phrases.english: Rava said:
You do not find a young scholar who gives halachic rulings
unless he comes from the tribe of Levi
or from the tribe of Issachar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לָא מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ צוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן דְּמוֹרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side teaching connected to the verse quoted in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scholars who give הוראה come from לוי or יששכר.

steps.title: Verses for לוי and יששכר
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a verse for each tribe: 'יורו משפטיך ליעקב' for לוי, and 'יודעי בינה לעתים' for יששכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: For לוי it is written: 'They shall teach Your laws to Jacob.' For יששכר it is written: 'The children of Issachar, who know how to understand the times, to know what Israel should do.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא proves his claim with one verse for each tribe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about לוי says they teach the law. The verse about יששכר says they understand the times and know what ישראל should do. Both verses describe giving practical guidance.

phrases.english: Levi, as it is written:
"They shall teach Your laws to Jacob."
Issachar, as it is written:
"And the children of Issachar, who know how to understand the times,
to know what Israel should do."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the sources for רבא's claim.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim about לוי and יששכר
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים לג:י and דברי הימים א יב:לג

steps.title: What about יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא left out יהודה, since a verse calls יהודה 'my lawgiver'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say יהודה as well, since it is written: 'Judah is my lawgiver'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's list as incomplete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse 'יהודה מחוקקי' shows that יהודה also produces lawgivers. So limiting the list to לוי and יששכר seems wrong.

phrases.english: But say Judah also,
as it is written: "Judah is my lawgiver"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's list from steps 11–12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that only לוי and יששכר produce scholars who give rulings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A verse describes יהודה as a lawgiver, so יהודה should be on the list too.

steps.title: Reaching the final הלכה
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that he meant people who can bring a discussion to the final practical הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: I was speaking about bringing a teaching up to the final הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains what he meant: not scholarship in general, but the skill of reaching the final ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהודה does produce great Torah scholars. However, the special skill of turning a discussion into a practical ruling belongs to לוי and יששכר. The question is answered by narrowing the meaning of 'מורי'.

keyTerms.meaning: bringing a teaching to its conclusion

steps.whatToRemember: There is a difference between general Torah greatness (יהודה) and the skill of reaching the final practical ruling (לוי and יששכר).

phrases.english: I was speaking of bringing a teaching up to the final halacha.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the meaning of the original statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'מורי' means any scholar, so יהודה should be included.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'מורי' means one who reaches the final הלכה, and that refers to לוי and יששכר.

steps.title: No separate lottery for the afternoon תמיד
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that there was no new פיס for the afternoon תמיד. The כהן who won a job in the morning does it again in the afternoon.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: They do not hold a lottery for the afternoon תמיד. Instead, the כהן who won a job in the morning wins it for the afternoon too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the topic of the lotteries with a new ruling from רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The morning פיס covers both the morning and afternoon תמיד. This means the same כהנים do the same jobs twice in one day.
steps.confusionAlert: This ruling covers the jobs of the תמיד, not the קטורת. Step 5 already taught that the קטורת always went to a new כהן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְפַיְּיסִין עַל תָּמִיד שֶׁל בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם,
phrases.english: They do not hold a lottery for the afternoon daily offering,
rather, the priest who won it in the morning
wins it for the afternoon,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵין מְפַיְּיסִין עַל תָּמִיד שֶׁל בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the topic of the lotteries after the side topic about the tribes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no separate פיס for the afternoon תמיד. The morning winners repeat their jobs.

steps.title: A ברייתא says there was an afternoon lottery
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן from a ברייתא saying they held a פיס in the afternoon just like in the morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: Just as they hold a lottery in the morning, so they hold a lottery in the afternoon!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's ruling using a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא openly says there was an afternoon פיס. That seems to contradict רבי יוחנן, who said there was none.

keyTerms.meaning: they raised an objection (from a ברייתא)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Just as they hold a lottery in the morning,
so too they hold a lottery in the afternoon!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that there was no afternoon פיס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא states that there was an afternoon פיס.

steps.title: That ברייתא refers to the incense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about the קטורת, which did get a new פיס every time.
steps.simpleTranslation: When that ברייתא was taught, it was about the קטורת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן by saying the ברייתא speaks about a different job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 taught that the קטורת always went to a new כהן, so it needed a new פיס in the afternoon. The jobs of the תמיד did not, which fits רבי יוחנן's ruling.

phrases.english: When that was taught, it was about the incense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא refers to the jobs of the תמיד.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא refers to the קטורת.

steps.title: A ברייתא says 'for it' in the masculine
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא says 'לו', a masculine word. That fits the תמיד (masculine) and not the קטורת (feminine).
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: Just as they hold a lottery for it (לו) in the morning, so they hold a lottery for it (לו) in the afternoon!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again with a ברייתא whose wording seems to block the last answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קטורת is a feminine noun, so 'for it' would be 'לה'. The masculine 'לו' points to the תמיד, so this ברייתא seems to describe an afternoon פיס for the תמיד.

keyTerms.meaning: but wasn't it taught (in a ברייתא)

steps.confusionAlert: The whole challenge depends on grammar: 'לו' is masculine (תמיד) and 'לה' is feminine (קטורת).

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught:
Just as they hold a lottery for it (masculine) in the morning,
so too they hold a lottery for it (masculine) in the afternoon!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the afternoon פיס refers to the קטורת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The masculine 'לו' points to the תמיד, not the feminine קטורת.

steps.title: Read it as 'for her'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording to 'לה' (feminine), so the ברייתא is also about the קטורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say 'לה' (for it, feminine).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of the ברייתא so that it fits רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the feminine 'לה', the ברייתא refers to the קטורת, just like the first ברייתא. רבי יוחנן's ruling stands: there was no separate afternoon פיס for the תמיד.

keyTerms.meaning: say / read it as (amends the text)

steps.whatToRemember: For now, רבי יוחנן's ruling stands: the morning פיס covers the afternoon תמיד, and only the קטורת gets a new פיס in the afternoon. The next ברייתא will challenge this, and the answer will limit an afternoon פיס for the תמיד to שבת.

phrases.english: Say "for it" (feminine).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 18 by changing the wording.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read 'לה', which refers to the קטורת.

steps.title: A ברייתא that says both 'for it (masculine)' and 'for it (feminine)'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that has two lines, one with 'לו' and one with 'לה'. This shows an afternoon פיס for both the תמיד and the קטורת, which goes against רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: Just as they hold a פיס for it (masculine) in the morning, so too they hold a פיס for it (masculine) in the afternoon. And just as they hold a פיס for it (feminine) in the morning, so too they hold a פיס for it (feminine) in the afternoon!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more ברייתא to challenge רבי יוחנן. This one cannot be explained away by changing one word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 19 the גמרא changed 'לו' to 'לה' so that the ברייתא was only about the קטורת. Here the ברייתא says both 'לו' and 'לה' side by side. So 'לו' must mean the תמיד and 'לה' must mean the קטורת. That means there was an afternoon פיס for the תמיד too, which goes against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא? (opens a challenge)
For it (masculine, the תָּמִיד) / for it (feminine, the קְטֹרֶת)
Afternoon or evening (here, the afternoon תָּמִיד)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not try to 'fix' this ברייתא the way we fixed the last one. Because both words appear together, changing 'לו' to 'לה' would just repeat the same line twice. That is why the גמרא needs a different answer.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא:
Just as they hold a lottery for it (masc.) in the morning
so too they hold a lottery for it (masc.) in the afternoon,
and just as they hold a lottery for it (fem.) in the morning
so too they hold a lottery for it (fem.) in the afternoon!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא that blocks the word change from Step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that there was no afternoon פיס for the תמיד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists 'לו' and 'לה' separately, so it must mean two different things: the תמיד and the קטורת. That means there was an afternoon פיס for the תמיד.

steps.title: The ברייתא is talking about שבת, when the priestly groups switch
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק answers that the ברייתא is about שבת. On שבת a new משמר of כהנים takes over in the middle of the day, so the afternoon תמיד needs its own פיס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק said: Here we are dealing with שבת, because the priestly groups (משמרות) change over then.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the ברייתא is about one special day, שבת, and not about every day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משמרות switch every שבת. The outgoing group does the morning service and the incoming group does the afternoon service. The morning winner belongs to the group that is leaving, so he cannot do the afternoon job, and a new פיס is needed. On regular days רבי יוחנן's rule still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Here we are dealing with שַׁבָּת
The priestly groups that take turns serving in the בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ week by week
Are renewed, a new group starts

steps.whyThisMatters: This saves רבי יוחנן's rule. Normally the morning winner does the afternoon תמיד too. שבת is an exception only because a different group of כהנים is serving in the afternoon.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said:
Here we are dealing with Shabbat,
since the priestly rotations are renewed then.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 20 by limiting the ברייתא to שבת
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to a special day
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to describe an afternoon פיס for the תמיד every day
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא describes only שבת, when a new משמר serves in the afternoon. On regular days there is no new פיס for the תמיד.

steps.title: How could we have thought there was a daily afternoon פיס? That makes too many lotteries
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא looks back at its earlier assumption that there was an afternoon פיס for the תמיד every day. That would make more than the four lotteries listed in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to what we thought at first, there would be too many lotteries!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions its own starting assumption. How could it ever have thought there was a daily afternoon פיס for the תמיד?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה clearly says there were four lotteries a day. If the תמיד had a second פיס every afternoon, there would be more than four. So the earlier idea seems impossible from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: According to what we first thought

phrases.english: And according to what we thought initially,
there would be too many lotteries!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the earlier assumption behind Steps 16 and 20 and asks how it could have worked
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier assumption that there was a daily afternoon פיס for the תמיד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה counts only four daily lotteries. A separate afternoon פיס would add to that count.

steps.title: All the כהנים gathered once in the morning to decide both jobs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the earlier idea. All the כהנים would come together once in the morning, and both the morning winner and the afternoon winner would be picked at that one gathering, so no extra פיס is added.
steps.simpleTranslation: They would all come together in the morning. The one who won the morning job got the morning job, and the one who won the afternoon job got the afternoon job.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. It shows that the first idea did not really add lotteries.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier idea, the afternoon job was also decided at the morning gathering. At that one gathering, the morning job would go to one כהן and the afternoon job to another. Since this happened at the same morning gathering, the count of four lotteries stays the same.

keyTerms.meaning: Wins, gets the right to the job

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: on a regular day the morning winner of the תמיד also does the afternoon תמיד (רבי יוחנן). The קטורת always gets a new פיס. On שבת there is a new afternoon פיס because a new משמר serves. Even the earlier idea did not add to the four lotteries, because both jobs would have been decided in the morning.

phrases.english: All of them would come in the morning,
whoever won it for the morning, won the morning,
whoever won for the afternoon, won the afternoon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining how the lottery would have been run
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A daily afternoon פיס would mean a fifth lottery
steps.terutzMaskana: Both winners would be picked at one morning gathering, so the number of lotteries stays at four

steps.title: Our משנה about the fourth lottery does not follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's fourth פיס, which was open to new and experienced כהנים. It then states that this משנה does not follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'The fourth lottery was for new ones together with old ones, etc.' Our משנה is not like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the next line of the משנה and makes a statement about it, which it will prove in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fourth פיס picked who would carry the limbs from the ramp up to the מזבח. That means the משנה holds this was a separate job from bringing the limbs to the ramp. The גמרא says this does not fit רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's view.

keyTerms.meaning: New כֹּהֲנִים together with old ones (those who already did the service)
Our מִשְׁנָה is not like the view of...

phrases.english: The fourth: new ones together with old ones, etc.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב.
phrases.english: Our mishna is not in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's fourth פיס, which separates carrying the limbs to the מזבח from carrying them to the ramp, does not match רבי אליעזר בן יעקב

steps.title: Proof: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says the same כהן brings the limbs all the way up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה where רבי אליעזר בן יעקב rules that the כהן who brings the limbs to the ramp also brings them up to the מזבח. So he would not need a separate fourth פיס.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: The one who brings the limbs up to the ramp is the one who brings them up to the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves its statement from Step 24 by quoting what רבי אליעזר בן יעקב actually says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, one כהן does both parts of the job. The כהן who won the second פיס and carried the limbs to the ramp would also carry them up to the מזבח. Our משנה gives the second part its own fourth פיס, so it must disagree with him.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a מִשְׁנָה
The ramp leading up to the מִזְבֵּחַ

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
The one who takes the limbs up to the ramp,
he is the one who takes them up to the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim in Step 24
steps.raayaObject: The claim that our משנה does not follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מסכת תמיד where רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says one כהן carries the limbs both to the ramp and to the מזבח

steps.title: The root of the disagreement: honoring the King vs. proper respect
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the two sides really disagree about. The תנא of the משנה follows 'בְּרׇב עָם הַדְרַת מֶלֶךְ', so more כהנים should take part. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds that splitting the job between people is not proper conduct in the מקום שכינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the basis of their disagreement? One Sage holds: 'In a crowd of people is the King's glory.' The other Sage holds: in the place of the Divine Presence, this is not proper behavior.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב disagree about a separate פיס for carrying the limbs up to the מזבח, and then answers its own question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's view gives one כהן the job of bringing the limbs to the ramp and another כהן the job of bringing them up to the מזבח, because more participants bring more honor to ה׳‎. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says that passing the limbs to someone else looks like the first כהן cannot be bothered to finish the job. That would be disrespectful in the place where the שכינה rests. So the same כהן does both, and no fourth פיס is needed for this job.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? (asking for the underlying reason of a dispute)
In a crowd of people is the King's glory (משלי יד:כח)
The place of the Divine Presence (the מקדש)
Not proper conduct; not respectful behavior

steps.whyThisMatters: Both sides want to honor ה׳. They only disagree about which arrangement shows more honor.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is not against involving many כהנים in general. His objection is to the specific case of one כהן handing off a job he has already started.

phrases.english: With regard to what do they disagree?
One Sage holds:
'In the multitude of people is the King's glory'
And the other Sage holds:
In the place of the Divine Presence it is not proper conduct.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the dispute that was just shown in step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה values many participants ('בְּרׇב עָם'). רבי אליעזר בן יעקב sees a hand-off as disrespectful in the מקום שכינה.

steps.title: רבא: Two Sages cannot share each other's opinions
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב cannot agree with רבי יהודה, and רבי יהודה cannot agree with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. If they agreed, there would be too few lotteries.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב does not hold like רבי יהודה, and רבי יהודה does not hold like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. For if so, they would be missing lotteries.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא makes a rule about how the opinions fit together, so that the total stays at four פייסות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי יהודה said there was no separate פיס for the מחתה (the coal pan). Now רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says there was no separate פיס for bringing the limbs up to the מזבח. If one Sage dropped both lotteries, only three would remain, but everyone agrees there were four. So רבי אליעזר בן יעקב must have had a פיס for the מחתה, and רבי יהודה must have had a פיס for bringing the limbs up.

keyTerms.meaning: They are lacking; there are too few
Lotteries used to assign Temple jobs

steps.whatToRemember: Every view must reach four פייסות. Each Sage drops one possible lottery, so each one must keep the other.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov does not
hold the view of Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה: no separate פיס for the מחתה

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda does not

phrases.aramaic: אִית לֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב.
phrases.english: hold the view of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov.
For if so, the lotteries would be too few.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אִית לֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's view and connects it to רבי יהודה's earlier view about the מחתה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and רבי יהודה cannot hold each other's views, because together they would leave only three lotteries.

steps.title: Opening: What about a תנא who counts five lotteries?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new thought about a תנא who teaches that there were five lotteries. The sentence finishes on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you find a תנא who teaches five —
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting to identify which Sage could hold of five lotteries, and the answer comes on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following רבא's logic, a count of five would come from a view that keeps both lotteries: the one for the מחתה and the one for bringing the limbs up. This line opens that identification but does not finish it yet.

keyTerms.meaning: A Sage of the משנה or ברייתא era

phrases.english: And if you find a Tanna
who teaches five (lotteries) —
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next עמוד

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבא's counting logic to explain a source that lists five lotteries.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces how to identify a תנא who counts five lotteries. The identification itself comes on the next עמוד.
